open_obligations: Note the small 7B-to-14B gap, which Lang et al. list as a limitation.
Check that AnthropicHH as binary classification is comparable to Burns et al.'s ChatGPT reward modeling task.
Check that baselines were reimplemented faithfully on Qwen models.
in.other_title: Debate-augmented weak supervisor raises PGR over strong-student baselines on four tasks
in.rationale: Burns et al. state none of their methods work consistently and the reward modeling gap is far from recovered. Lang, Huang and Li report their debate-ensemble method raises PGR over finetuning with auxiliary confidence loss on all four tasks, e.g. CosmosQA 17.4% to 56.5% and AnthropicHH 35.0% to 70.0%; models are Qwen-7B and Qwen-14B, a small compute gap.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether weak-to-strong methods can recover more of the performance gap, for debate-augmented weak supervisors on NLP classification

text: The authors state that none of their methods work consistently in all settings, that especially in the reward modeling setting they remain far from recovering the full performance gap between weak and strong models, and that their methods are proofs-of-concept that weak-to-strong generalization is tractable rather than practical solutions recommended for deployment.
title: No weak-to-strong method works consistently; reward modeling gap far from recovered
